Action.description: A typed action a client asks for (GUI buttons, hosts); the kernel dispatches it to a command.

key.description: A single-key hint; the surface may use another key.

ActionItem.description: A button: the surface fires `Input::Action` with `action` (ADR-0008 §1).

name.description: One file or directory name, without a separator.

oneOf.description:
The options ticked and, beside them, the words a person typed of their
own (M59): a question may be answered both ways at once, and dropping
either half loses what they said. An old frame carries no `other` and
reads as the ticks alone. Words with nothing ticked are
[`Answer::Text`], which is what a question answered in words alone has
always been.

A form's answers, one per question in the order they were asked; a
question nobody answered is [`Answer::Cancel`] in its place (M53).
"Let it happen."
The refusal a question falls to when nobody answers it.

AnswerRole.description:
The two options a session may answer a question with when nobody is asked
(ADR-0039 §2). The asker names them in its own words; the kernel reads
which is which and never the words.

plugin.description: The plugin that owns the record.

kind.description: The record's kind, named by its plugin.

oneOf.description: An argument followed by optional flags, completed from the same spec.
Completed from a catalog kind the command validates against.

alone.description: Words among `values` that end the argument; `then` does not apply.

person.description:
Words among `values` only the person may run: they raise trust or
let repository code run, so no link rewrites a line that starts
with one and no view bingo did not draw may send one.

oneOf.description:
One of the words the command lists itself, in the order it offers
them. A surface completes from the list; the kernel carries it.

`then` says what the word after one of `values` is — the name
`/plugins enable` takes, the server `/mcp reconnect` takes — and is
absent for a command whose argument ends at the first word, so every
spec written before it reads the same (ADR-0008 §6a).

call.description: The `callId` this process was given in `tool/call`.

AskParams.description:
`bingo.host.ask`: a question from the process, on one of its running calls.

The call names the crossing and is the whole of the grant: the bridge
already tracks running calls, an ended one is not there to ask on, and
another connection's is not this caller's to reach (ADR-0033 §3 as
amended). Nothing is minted for it.

The question is the sdk's own `InteractionKind`, so the person is asked by
the machinery every in-process tool's question rides. Only a question
crosses: a permission, a confirmation or a login is the host's own to open,
and a grant is never Allow-shaped.

AskResult.description:
What the person answered, as the sdk writes it — including the cancel that
is an answer.

kind.description: What kind of question it is.

answers.description: The answers the person may give.

oneOf.description: The holding command that asked has finished (ADR-0012 §5).

call.description: The call as judged, possibly with tightened arguments.

ChoiceScope.description: Whether the chosen model applies only here or is the default for new sessions.

labels.description: The labels the model chooses from.

into.description: Destination command shown in the palette for the folded names.

names.description: Command names or aliases found through the destination without changing dispatch.

CommandFold.description: Commands presented through one destination while their dispatch stays intact.

oneOf.description: Forward an existing command result without recording or executing it again.
A client interprets only actions it supports; the host does not dispatch them.
A site key chose an answer; the surface decides whether to send it.
Becomes a turn, submitted with the command's own intent and origin.

One completed item the kernel records in the transcript (a shell
line's output, a login's receipt); the ack carries its id.

anyOf.description: Applied, with `text` shown as its message.

surface.description: The surface the command was typed on, when known.

command.description: The command's name, without the slash.

args.description: The rest of the line after the name.

CommandRunParams.description: One `/name args` line, with the argument text exactly as it was typed.

opens.description:
Run bare, it opens the place where its argument is chosen, so a
palette runs it rather than listing `args`; `args` stays for every
surface that completes it.

hint.description: A one-line description for the command menu; argument syntax belongs in `args`.

instant.description: May run while a turn is busy (read-only commands).

CompactError.description: A rejected summary still bills any usage observed before it failed.

usage.description: The context reading that triggered it.

request.description: The request the next round would send.

keepBudget.description: Tokens of recent history to keep verbatim.

CompactReason.description:
Why a compaction was asked for. Serializable because a strategy may live in
another process: the reason crosses the bridge as it is.

usage.description: What the summary cost. A strategy that spends no tokens says nothing.

Compaction.description:
The result: a summary, the boundary before which items are replaced, the
items before it to keep anyway, and what the summary cost. The kernel
accepts it only when `after < before`; the cost is billed either way.

id.description: Which of the compactors the handshake declared is being asked.

CompactorCompactResult.description:
Declared failures retain observed usage; generic transport errors cannot
report what a process spent before the connection failed.

failures.description:
Consecutive compactions the kernel discarded; at `BREAKER_TRIP` the
breaker is tripped and a strategy takes its rung that needs no model.

keepBudget.description: Tokens of the newest items a cut should leave intact.

CompactorContext.description:
What a compaction acts on, as a process that is not in the host can read
it: the sdk's `CompactContext` without what cannot cross — the host's
provider and the turn's cancellation token. A remote strategy summarises by
its own means, or cuts by none.

CompactorSpec.description:
A compaction strategy a process says it has. One field, and the same shape
as every other declaration: a plugin's answer to "what do you contribute"
reads the same way whatever the kind.

ConfigView.description: Configuration as a client sees it: the kernel's keys and each plugin's claimed slice.

id.description: Which of the contributors the handshake declared is being asked.

pieces.description:
A contributor with nothing to add this round says so with an empty
list, which is never wrong.

oneOf.description:
Recorded as a user item with `Origin { surface: "contributor:<id>" }`, so
the transcript and the provider cache prefix agree.

ContextPiece.description:
What a contributor adds. Serializable for the same reason a placement is:
a piece written in another process crosses as it is, never as a copy of
itself the bridge invented.

parts.description: Approximate local request composition, independent of server anchoring.

used.description: Tokens the next request would carry, anchored on the server's last count.

window.description:
The input side of the model's window: what is left once the output
budget is reserved (ADR-0006).

trigger.description:
`used` at which the older turns are summarised, equal to `window`
where the kernel draws no line because the endpoint holds the context
and cuts it itself (ADR-0055 §2).

ContextUsage.description:
The one ruler for context: used tokens, the model window, and the point at
which compaction triggers.

ContributeQuery.description:
One round, as a process that is not in the host can read it.

The serializable projection of the sdk's `ContextQuery` (ADR-0030 §5): the
session, where it is and what it has said so far. The host handle the
in-process query carries stays on this side — an external contributor
reads the round, it does not reach the host.

id.description:
The name this process knows the contributor by; `context/contribute`
carries it back. The kernel sees it prefixed by the plugin's own name.

ContributorSpec.description:
A contributor a process says it has. Placement is handshake data: which of
the three moments this contributor speaks at is asked once, here, and never
per call. A placement this host does not know refuses the handshake, in
words, rather than being guessed at.

scope.description: The narrowest rule that would silence this prompt, offered as "allow for session".

oneOf.description: An idle target opens a turn on it; a busy one absorbs it at the next barrier.
It waits in the queue for whatever opens the next turn.

Delivery.description:
How a line reaches a session's queue: a peer's message (ADR-0010 §1) and
a person's own line are the same question, so they are the same word.

oneOf.description: Append to assistant text.
Append to reasoning text.
Replace the progress tail of a running tool call.
A model answers: every prose input opens a turn.
Nothing answers: every input is recorded, and the journal is the point.

Driver.description: What a session does with what it is told (ADR-0011 §1).

Effort.description: Reasoning effort, in the vocabulary providers converge on.

contextWindow.description:
The window this endpoint last named for this model. A server's word on
itself outranks every guess at it (ADR-0055 §2).

EndpointCapabilities.description:
What an endpoint does with a request, as only the provider can know:
whether image parts reach the model, whether tokens can be counted ahead,
whether prefixes are cached, whether the conversation is its own. The
model's own facts — window, output budget, reasoning, vision — are the
kernel catalogue's (ADR-0004).

env.description: Added to the host's environment, never replacing it.

oneOf.description: The person stopped it; not a failure.
A negotiated RPC byte or pin budget cannot carry this value safely.

What was named is not there any more: a queued line a turn has taken
(ADR-0008 §2, amended M68).
The store could not read or write; the disk, not the kernel.

anyOf.description:
Where the context stands outside a round: published when a segment
opens and when the model changes, once the window is known. `None`
says the window is no longer known.
Additive model spend, independent of context measurement and rounds.
Ephemeral. `ItemCompleted` is authoritative over every delta before it.
A plugin-owned resource changed (roster, room, task…). The kernel does not enumerate these.

Ephemeral. A plugin's live state (ADR-0013 §2): the latest payload per
`(plugin, kind)` is the whole of it; `Null` removes it; none survives a resume.
Ephemeral, transport only: this subscriber missed `from..=to`; re-read the journal.
A payload this build cannot read, carried without interpretation.

truncated.description: Whether the body was cut at the host's limit.

notice.description: A note from the host about the fetch, if any.

path.description: Relative to the session's cwd, or absolute under a granted root.
Relative to the session's cwd, or absolute under a granted root.

file.description: Whether it is a regular file.

path.description: Relative to the session's cwd, or absolute under a granted root.

cause.description: The client intent this frame answers or results from, when there is one.

oversized.description:
This item alone cannot fit the requested page. Fetch it explicitly in
parts before following `next`, which excludes that item.

maxBytes.description:
Optional byte budget for the whole JSON-RPC response; absent preserves
`limit == 0` meaning all, not an implicit bounded page.

generation.description: Reject a stale page after a rewind/compaction rather than mixing views.

id.description: Which of the hooks the handshake declared is watching.

HookObserveParams.description: Kernel → plugin: one observation point happened. Nothing is awaited.

HookSite.description:
Where a hook is standing, as a process that is not in the host can read it.

The serializable projection of the sdk's `HookContext` (ADR-0030 §5): which
session, which turn if any, where it works and what model answers it. The
host handle and the provider stay on this side — an external hook reads
where it is, it does not reach the host.

id.description:
The name this process knows the hook by; `hook/observe` carry it back. The kernel sees it prefixed by the
plugin's own name.

tool.description: Exact tool name or a trailing `*` prefix for the tool points.

HookSpec.description:
A hook a process says it has, and the matcher it is claimed with.

The matcher is the sdk's own, declared once: the kernel's cheap skip runs
on this side, so an event this matcher rules out never crosses the pipe at
all (ADR-0032 §1). A declaration that names no point wants every point, as
an in-process hook's empty matcher does.

HostEnv.description:
Where the host lives, as a process that is not in it can read.

A projection of the sdk's `Env`, which is not `Serialize`: a plugin that
keeps state of its own needs somewhere to put it, and `dataDir` is where.

path.description:
Where the same bytes are on this machine, when they are anywhere: a
picture read off a disk, or one a surface wrote before handing it on
(ADR-0052). A location, not a second copy — absent from the wire and
the journal when there is none, so a picture without one is the
bytes it always was.

Image.description:
A picture handed to the model, already the shape the journal keeps and a
provider's request encodes: one struct, so a surface that reads a picture
off disk, a wire client that already holds the bytes, and a tool result
that returns one all produce the same thing.

pluginRoot.description: The directory the manifest was read from, already resolved.

config.description: This plugin's settings slice (`plugins.<name>`); `null` when unset.

InitializeParams.description: The handshake, sent once on a fresh process.

protocol.description:
The major the process speaks. The host refuses any but its own, which
it can only do if the process says which one it is.

services.description:
The services this process serves, by the key another plugin calls them
by. A key is global — it is what a consumer writes in `requires` — so
the declaration is a map and not a list: one answer per key.

InitializeResult.description:
What the process says it is and what it contributes. Everything here is a
claim: the tools it names are registered untrusted (ADR-0015 §4).

images.description:
The pictures the ask carries, in the order they reach the journal
(ADR-0040): exactly as they will be journaled, because a surface
resolves a picture and the kernel does no file I/O for input.

delivery.description:
Whether a running turn may be steered with it (ADR-0008 §2,
amended M68). `Wake` is the line every client has always sent, so
it is the default and nothing is written for it.

origin.description:
The door it came through. Absent, or a door that is not a person
surface, and the action is not the person's own: it fails closed.

Input.description:
The one submission entry. The kernel parses `/`, `!` and `@` in text and
decides turn, queue, steer or deliver; a client never chooses.

IntentId.description: A client-minted write id; the outcome arrives as `IntentAck`.

guardUntil.description: Keyboard approvals before this instant are rejected with `NOT_READY`.

answers.description: Exactly the answers the kernel will accept.

InteractionId.description: A pending question or permission, answered once by id.

input.description: The call after hooks and interceptors, before this decision.

sessionScope.description: The rule `AllowSession` would install, when one would silence the prompt.

oneOf.description:
One question on its own. It holds [`Question`] flattened, so the frame
it makes is the one it always was.

title.description:
What the whole set is about, in the asker's own words: an MCP
server's elicitation says which server is asking. A set the model
opened has nothing to add to its own questions and names none.

oneOf.description:
A set of questions put at once and answered together (M53). Every
question is the same [`Question`] a lone one is.

intent.description: The client intent that produced this item, when one did (user items).

anyOf.description:
A shell line a person ran themselves (`!<command>`, ADR-0008 §5): no
turn was spent on it and no model asked for it. `exit` is the code the
command came to; `None` says it never reached one — its timeout or an
interrupt ended it, and `output` carries the line that says which.
A long-running non-turn operation (login, reconnect, team start).
A payload this build cannot read, carried without interpretation.

ItemId.description: One unit in the transcript order.

KernelError.description: An error as it appears on the wire and in the journal.

KeyBinding.description:
A chord a command declares for itself. A bare chord runs the command
alone; one with `args` submits the command with them, so a shortcut for
`/model next` is a binding on `model` and not a second catalogue entry.

Length.description:
A length: a number of terminal cells, or a share of the screen written as
a percentage string such as `'40%'`.

render.description: Per-hook render partials, when one link contains several hooks.

Manifest.description:
What one directory under `plugins/` declares about itself.

Unknown keys are kept rather than refused: a manifest written for a later
host must still start on this one.

name.description:
What the plugin calls itself. It must be the name of the directory
holding it: the path is what one layer overrides another by, so two
spellings of the name would be two answers to "which plugin is this".

config.description:
A JSON Schema for this plugin's own settings — the slice a person
writes under `plugins.<name>`, which reaches the process as
`initialize.config`. It is what a person reads; nothing in this
workspace validates a document against a schema.

callTimeout.description: Maximum seconds for tool/call and command/run; absent allows ten minutes.

name.description:
What the plugin calls itself. It must be the name of the directory
holding it: the path is what one layer overrides another by, so two
spellings of the name would be two answers to "which plugin is this".

config.description:
A JSON Schema for this plugin's own settings — the slice a person
writes under `plugins.<name>`, which reaches the process as
`initialize.config`. It is what a person reads; nothing in this
workspace validates a document against a schema.

callTimeout.description: Maximum seconds for tool/call and command/run; absent allows ten minutes.

ModelCapabilities.description:
What a turn may assume about its model: the kernel's resolution of the
user's settings, the catalogue, the server's corrections and the
endpoint's facts (ADR-0004). The ruler and the gate read this.

oneOf.description: The complete call. `input` is the raw JSON text; the loop parses it once.

What the endpoint says it is holding for this session: its own count,
against its own window (ADR-0055 §2). Sent as often as it likes; the
last one of a round is what that round reports.

A cut the endpoint made in the context it holds (ADR-0055 §3). The
journal lost nothing by it: it is a row, not a rewrite.

ModelEvent.description: Provider stream events. Never published; the accumulator folds them into items.

selected.description: The chosen row's key; its position is found again on every drawing.

session.description:
Whose turn this is. A stateless provider ignores it; one that keeps a
conversation of its own per session — an ACP adapter holding one agent
session per bingo session (ADR-0035 §3), a stateful wire like the
Responses API — has no other way to know which conversation it is
answering. `None` is a request built by hand or a side question, which
belongs to no session.

NoticeParams.description:
`bingo.host.notice`: one line for the person, under the plugin's own name.

The one door that is scoped by nothing (ADR-0033 §4): it spends nothing but
a line, so it needs no crossing to belong to. The level is the kernel's own
three and nothing else can be written; an omitted one is the quietest.

NoticeResult.description: A notice is told, not asked: there is nothing to answer with.

renderSurface.description: Drawing family of the caller, independent of its attribution identifier.

Origin.description: Who submitted the input, as every surface records it.

checksum.description: FNV-1a 64 of the exact serialized Item UTF-8, lowercase hex.

OversizedItem.description:
The actor's factual observation; only the RPC server can add a
connection-scoped availability token after pinning an immutable Item.

catalogs.description:
Only the catalogues the query's command completes from, once the
query reaches its arguments: every press carries them, and a model
catalogue is the largest thing it would otherwise carry.

PaletteSession.description: A compact row, projected by the client from live or stored facts.

PanePlace.description:
Where a pane sits: `'above'` the prompt, at the `'side'`, as an
`'overlay'` floating over the screen, or at a fixed `{rect}`.

PaneSize.description: A pane's height and width; each defaults when left out.

ParentLink.description:
Where a child hangs in the tree: its parent, and the tool call that
spawned it when one did (ADR-0011 §3).

slot.description: The plugin's placement key. Several independent slots can coexist.

oneOf.description: A system block, recomputed per request; lower `order` first.
A user piece at the start of each round.
A user piece after tool results, before the next request.

Placement.description:
When a contributor speaks. Serializable because a contributor may live in
another process: it declares its placement once, over the bridge.

argv.description: The program and its arguments; no shell is involved.

cwd.description: Working directory; the session's cwd unless given.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the process after this many milliseconds.

code.description: The exit code, or `null` when killed by a signal.

queue.description: Inputs waiting for the next turn.

ProviderCancelParams.description:
Kernel → plugin: nobody is reading this stream any more — the turn was
interrupted, or whoever asked let go. A process that ignores it is slow, not
broken: the host stops reading either way, and the stream's idle deadline is
what keeps a silent one from holding a turn open.

ProviderDeltaParams.description: Plugin → kernel, while a stream runs: one event, for one stream.

ProviderSpec.description:
A model provider a process says it serves, and the whole of what the host
believes about it. The id is the one a person types (`--provider <id>`,
`/model <id>/<model>`), `family` is the catalogue shelf its models are filed
under (ADR-0017; the id itself by default, as the sdk trait does), and
`models` is what it serves — the answer to `Provider::models`, given once
here so that asking costs no call.

`endpoint` is what this endpoint does with a request for one of *those*
models. A model the declaration does not name gets nothing: no images, no
token counting, no caching (ADR-0015 §4).

id.description: Which of the providers the handshake declared is being asked.

ProviderStreamParams.description:
One model response, asked for. The request crosses as the sdk writes it —
system blocks, messages, tools and all — because a provider that cannot read
the whole request cannot answer it.

`call` names this stream. Every [`ProviderDeltaParams`] carries it back and
[`ProviderCancelParams`] stops it by it, so two streams running on one pipe
never interleave.

ProviderStreamResult.description:
The close. A stream that ran to its `finish` event answers with nothing; one
that broke answers with the error the trait speaks, so the kernel's retry
ladder reads the same kind it reads from an in-process provider.

PullRequest.description: A placement has no asking surface until a client pulls it.

header.description: A short tag a surface may show before the question (`Auth method`).

Question.description:
One question put to a person: what is asked, what may be picked, and
whether words of one's own or more than one option count. A lone question
and one of a form are the same thing (M53).

QuestionFocus.description: A question owner's editing projection; sealed labels remain the host's.

role.description:
What picking it would mean to a session that answers for the person
(ADR-0039 §2). Unmarked options are a person's alone.

preview.description:
A few lines of monospace shown beside the option while the cursor is
on it — the layout or the snippet picking it would mean (M53).

Rect.description:
A fixed rectangle: `width` by `height`, offset by `x` and `y` from
`anchor`, a corner or the `center` (`topLeft` unless given).

requestId.description: Which instance of the site; for `Pane`, the id given to `$.ui.open`.

props.description: The site's facts; their shape is the component's props.

viewport.description: The cells the surface offers the drawing.

name.description: The command's name, without the slash.

delivery.description: Whether it wakes the receiver or waits for its next turn.

Seq.description:
Position of a frame in a session's journal. Durable frames are gapless;
clients only require monotonic order.

ServiceCallParams.description:
One call on one service, the same shape whichever way it goes: the key
that names the service, the method, and whatever that method takes.

Neither side reads `params`: it is the service's own contract, written in
the schema the declaration carries, and the bridge is a pipe for it.

ServiceCallResult.description:
What the service answered. A service with nothing to say answers `null`,
which is an answer; a service that could not answer fails the call.

ServiceSpec.description:
What one service speaks: a name for every method it answers, and the JSON
Schema of what that method takes.

The schema is for whoever writes the caller — nothing here validates
against it, as nothing validates a manifest's `config` schema — and the
names are the host's: a method the declaration never named is refused
before it crosses, with the set that is named (ADR-0031 §5). A service
that names no method speaks none.

session.description: The session this concerns; `$` methods default it to the current one.

SessionId.description: One persisted context: one journal, one actor.

systemExtra.description:
What the session was opened with and a resume must give it back:
the prompt appended to the kernel's own, and the tool set it is held to.

busy.description:
A turn is running. A summary travels without the turn it describes —
a host listing carries no `SessionState` — so the kernel stamps this
on every summary it publishes and nothing else writes it. A client
that holds the state derives the same fact with `SessionState::busy`.

asking.description: An interaction is open; stamped only by the session actor.

messages.description:
How many messages have been said in this session, by
[`Event::completes_a_message`]. `None` is "never counted" — a summary
written before the field existed — and must be shown as nothing rather
than as a `0` it does not mean.

session.description: The viewed session: it owns the opening and is the row marked current.

sessions.description: One extra summary is the sentinel for the next page.

current.description: The mode's value: the argument of the item that chooses it.

modes.description: The first label is the resting mode, which a surface may leave unsaid.

ideal.description: What it takes when there is room.

Span.description: A size the surface fits between `min` and `max`, preferring `ideal`.

StatusProps.description: Optional facts supplied by the asking surface, without transcript bodies.

oneOf.description: Let the turn end.

Keep the turn running; `reason` goes back to the model and `origin`
names who asked.

input.description: What to submit, as a person would type it.

oneOf.description: Admit this input, possibly changed.
Refuse it with this error.
Send it to another session instead.

SystemBlock.description: One cacheable segment of the system prompt.

TextChild.description: A text child preserves the style of its nested Text node.

oneOf.description: Wants a person: a surface makes it move.

Tone.description: The one styling hook a plugin has; the surface owns the colour.

ToolCall.description: A call the model asked for, before or after the gate.

anyOf.description: Refuse the call; `deny` is the reason the model reads.
The tool's output, from `next` or answered by the hook.

ToolCallAnswer.description: A denial is an answer, never an invalid output that falls through to execution.

ToolCallParams.description:
One call, named as the plugin named it — the `plugin__<name>__` prefix is
the model's and the permission grammar's, never the process's.

ToolCancelParams.description:
Kernel → plugin: this call's turn was interrupted, and nobody is waiting
for the answer any more. The host has already let the call go, so a process
that ignores this is not holding anything up — it is only doing work whose
result will be thrown away.

tool.description: The tool's name, such as `Bash` or `Edit`.

tool_use_id.description: The model's id for this call.

ToolEvent.description:
A tool call as a hook sees it: the tool's own arguments sit beside
`tool` and `tool_use_id`, not under an `input` field.

ToolOutput.description:
What a tool returned: the parts the model sees, plus what a person sees
instead when the tool has something better than the text (ADR-0013 §2).

ToolProgressParams.description: Plugin → kernel, while a call runs: the whole of the live output line.

meta.description:
What a catalogue may show beside the tool (an MCP tool's `server`);
never sent to a model.

ToolSpec.description: A tool as the model sees it.

Turn2.description:
One turn as a row: its headline only. The whole prompt stays in the
transcript, where `asked` reads it.

TurnId.description: One run of the turn loop, closed exactly once.

oneOf.description: A client submitted while the session was idle.
Drained from the queue when the previous turn ended.
Another session posted into this one.
The kernel or a plugin opened the turn with no prose.

Usage.description:
Token counts as the provider reports them, the three input counts kept
apart: `input_tokens` is what the model read fresh, the cache counts are
what it read from or wrote to a cached prefix. The whole input side is
`input_total()`.

session.description: Tokens used by the whole session.

context.description: The current context window reading, once known.

lastTurn.description: Tokens used by the last turn.

children.description: Strings and nested `Text` nodes, drawn in order.

color.description: A colour name or `#rrggbb`; the surface may adjust it to its theme.

inverse.description: Swap the foreground and background colours.

wrap.description: `wrap` breaks long lines at the width; `truncate` cuts them.

oneOf.description: A run of text: strings and nested `Text` nodes, which keep their own style.
Markdown text the surface renders.

language.description: The language name for highlighting, such as `rust`.

oneOf.description: A block of source code.
A diff drawn with added and removed lines marked.
A bulleted list of lines.

rows.description: One array of cells per row, in column order.

oneOf.description: A table of strings.
Aligned label and value pairs.

total.description: The whole; without it the surface shows a count.

oneOf.description: A progress bar, or a count when there is no total.

tone.description: `neutral`, `good`, `bad` or `attention`; the surface picks the colour.

oneOf.description: A short label coloured by its tone.
An indented tree of labelled nodes.

question.description:
A question owner's editing state, on the root of a drawn question;
the choices' labels and the answer stay the host's.

hints.description: The focused site declares chrome separately from its body.

onKey.description: A handler for a key pressed while this box's pane has focus; return `{handled: false}` to give the key back.

flexGrow.description: How much of the spare room this box takes; `0` takes none.

flexWrap.description: `wrap` lets children flow onto another line.

margin.description: Cells outside the box on every side.

marginX.description: Cells outside the box on the left and right.

marginY.description: Rows outside the box above and below.

padding.description: Cells inside the box on every side.

paddingX.description: Cells inside the box on the left and right.

paddingY.description: Rows inside the box above and below.

borderStyle.description: Any value but `none` draws a border.

display.description: `none` hides the box and its controls.

oneOf.description: A flex container: lays its children out in a row or a column.
One view under a title.
A row of buttons that each run a named action.

children.description: The button's text, when `label` is not given.

hotkey.description: One letter: pressed with Alt in a band, or alone in a focused pane, it presses the button.

variant.description: `primary` draws it bold, `danger` in the alarm colour.

onPress.description: The handler run when the button is pressed: a mod passes a function.

oneOf.description: A pressable control; a mod's `onPress` runs when it is pressed.

placeholder.description: Text shown while the field is empty.

onInput.description: The handler run as the text changes: a mod passes a function.

onSubmit.description: The handler run when the person presses Enter: a mod passes a function.

oneOf.description: A one-line text field.

onSelect.description: The handler run with the chosen value: a mod passes a function.

oneOf.description: A choice among options.

label.description: The text shown; the URL when absent.

oneOf.description: A link the person can open.

alt.description: Text shown where the image cannot be.

oneOf.description: A picture; surfaces that cannot draw it show `alt`.
A grid of character cells, drawn by terminals only.

alt.description: Text shown where the drawing cannot be.

oneOf.description: An SVG drawing, for surfaces that draw vectors; others show `alt`.

component.description: The component bingo draws, such as `ToolUse`.

props.description: That component's props, as its `ui.render` event carried them.

oneOf.description: bingo's own drawing of a component, placed inside a mod's view.

fold.description: The plain text drawn where the element is unknown.

oneOf.description: An element bingo has no name for; surfaces that do not know it show `fold`.

place.description: Where a pane sits, when the site is a pane.

Voice.description: How a producer intends an utterance to be drawn.
